title: America's first approved BWRX-300 could open a new nuclear race
source_used: TechRadar (pool link, fetched text); the issue date of the permit checked in Power Engineering, NEI Magazine and Neutron Bytes
key_facts: The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved a construction permit for the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) to build a 300-megawatt GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactor at its Clinch River site in Tennessee.
Power Engineering (1 Oct 2026) says the permit was issued on Tuesday, which was 29 Sep 2026; TechRadar's article is dated 6 Oct 2026.
TechRadar says the NRC completed its assessment in 14 months; TVA still needs another licence before loading fuel or generating electricity.
TVA is considering as many as four BWRX-300 units at the site, and construction timing remains undecided.
TVA's interim president Mike Skaggs called the permit foundational for America's nuclear future.

TechRadar adds that SGE proposes up to 14 of the reactors across three UK sites at about £35 billion, Ontario Power Generation is preparing a first unit, and Blue Energy has applied in Texas to supply data centers directly.
Developers expect repeating one design to cut costs, which TechRadar says remains unproven in the US, where recent large nuclear projects ran late and over budget.
quote_evidence: The United States has approved construction of a 300MW small modular reactor as electricity demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure continues rising.
However, the utility still requires another license before loading nuclear fuel or beginning electricity generation from the approved reactor unit.
That expectation remains unproven in America, where recent large nuclear developments have experienced substantial delays and costs exceeding initial estimates.
why_it_matters_hint: A first US permit for a small modular reactor design that developers hope can supply steady power to data centers, though it does not allow operation and the cost savings are unproven.
event_date: Permit issued Tuesday 29 Sep 2026; TechRadar article dated 6 Oct 2026.
notes: Older news re-dated: the permit was reported on 30 Sep and 1 Oct 2026 by Neutron Bytes, Power Engineering, NEI Magazine and others. Not in our earlier reports or in the pools of the last four days, so readers have not seen it. NEI says the review ended four months ahead of schedule.
